req.title: Include Content-Length on echo responses
req.statement: The system shall include a Content-Length header equal to the response body byte length on echo endpoints.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that echo endpoints (/get, /post, /put, /patch, /delete) include a Content-Length header whose value exactly equals the byte length of the response body. Tests must: (1) verify the header is present and numerically correct for each method (positive/EP), (2) verify the header value matches len(response.data) exactly — not approximately (BVA), (3) verify that a body with non-ASCII/multi-byte content still produces a correct byte-length count (boundary), (4) verify wrong methods return 4xx without a misleading Content-Length (negative/NEG), and (5) verify the arithmetic identity Content-Length == len(data) holds for a zero-byte-body edge case (BVA boundary at 0). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting the exact integer value computed from the actual response body, so any off-by-one or sign-flip mutation in the header-setting code will cause the assertion to fail.

tests.name: test_get_content_length_exact_match
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_content_length_exact_match():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    body_len = len(r.data)
    assert cl == body_len
    assert cl > 0

test_get_content_length_exact_match()

tests.name: test_content_length_not_off_by_one_get
preconditions: GET /get endpoint returns a non-empty JSON body
expected: Content-Length does not equal byte_count minus 1
Content-Length does not equal byte_count plus 1
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_not_off_by_one_get():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body_len = len(r.data)
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl == body_len
    assert cl != body_len - 1
    assert cl != body_len + 1

test_content_length_not_off_by_one_get()

tests.name: test_content_length_with_query_params_get
preconditions: GET /get endpoint echoes query parameters in body
actions: Send GET /get?a=1&b=2 (body will be larger than plain /get)
expected: Content-Length reflects the larger body with echoed query params
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_with_query_params_get():
    r = client.get('/get?a=1&b=2')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body_len = len(r.data)
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl == body_len
    assert cl > 0
    r2 = client.get('/get')
    body_len2 = len(r2.data)
    cl2 = int(r2.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl2 == body_len2
    assert cl != cl2

test_content_length_with_query_params_get()

tests.name: test_content_length_is_integer_parseable
preconditions: All five echo endpoints are registered
actions: Send one request to each of /get /post /put /patch /delete
For each: parse Content-Length as int, compare to len(data)
expected: All five Content-Length values are valid integers equal to body byte length
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_is_integer_parseable():
    cases = [
        ('GET',    '/get',    {}),
        ('POST',   '/post',   {'data': 'x=1'}),
        ('PUT',    '/put',    {'data': 'x=1'}),
        ('PATCH',  '/patch',  {'data': 'x=1'}),
        ('DELETE', '/delete', {}),
    ]
    for method, path, kwargs in cases:
        r = client.open(path, method=method, **kwargs)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'{method} {path} got {r.status_code}'
        assert 'Content-Length' in r.headers, f'Missing Content-Length on {path}'
        cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
        body_len = len(r.data)
        assert cl == body_len, f'{method} {path}: CL={cl} body={body_len}'

test_content_length_is_integer_parseable()

tests.name: test_content_length_changes_with_body_size
preconditions: POST /post echoes request body in response
actions: Send POST /post with small body, record Content-Length
Send POST /post with larger body, record Content-Length
Assert second Content-Length > first and both equal len(response.data)
expected: Content-Length grows proportionally with echoed body
Both values equal their respective body byte lengths exactly
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_changes_with_body_size():
    r1 = client.post('/post', data='a=1')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    cl1 = int(r1.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl1 == len(r1.data)

    r2 = client.post('/post', data='a=' + 'x' * 200)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    cl2 = int(r2.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl2 == len(r2.data)

    assert cl2 > cl1

test_content_length_changes_with_body_size()

tests.name: test_content_length_header_name_case_insensitive_present
actions: Check that Content-Length header key exists (case-insensitive)
Verify value is a non-negative integer equal to body length
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_content_length_header_name_case_insensitive_present():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    header_keys_lower = [k.lower() for k in r.headers.keys()]
    assert 'content-length' in header_keys_lower
    cl = int(r.headers['Content-Length'])
    assert cl >= 0
    assert cl == len(r.data)

test_content_length_header_name_case_insensitive_present()
